item.title: Pensacola Interstate Fair Cuts Weekday Admission to $12, Offers Early-Bird Deals
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Pensacola Interstate Fair is bringing back budget-friendly admission this October, lowering weekday ticket prices and rolling out advance-purchase discounts ahead of its 11-day run from October 22 through November 1. Adult admission drops to $12 Monday through Thursday, down from the usual $14, while weekend prices hold at $14. Children ages…
item.content:encoded:
The Pensacola Interstate Fair is bringing back budget-friendly admission this October, lowering weekday ticket prices and rolling out advance-purchase discounts ahead of its 11-day run from October 22 through November 1.

Adult admission drops to $12 Monday through Thursday, down from the usual $14, while weekend prices hold at $14. Children ages 4–11 pay $6 weekdays, and kids 3 and under get in free any day. The Fair is also selling advance "Super Saver" tickets online through Wednesday, October 21—half off regular prices at $7 for adults and $3 for children—plus discounted parking at $5 and cut-rate ride wristbands ranging from $27 to $32 depending on day of use.

The Fair's opening day, Thursday, October 22, kicks off with a $1 admission special for ages 4 and up and $1 individual rides. The 11 days include live entertainment on the Pepsi Stage—featuring Hunter Hayes, The Band Perry, and Glenn Leonard's Temptations Revue—plus livestock shows, carnival rides, and farm-themed attractions. Special admission days are scattered throughout, including Military Appreciation Day (active and retired military pay $7), First Responders' Day, Teacher Tuesday, and Kids' Day with free admission for children 11 and under from 11 a.m. to 2 p.m. on Saturday, October 24.

Tickets and full details are available at PensacolaFair.com.

item.title: Santa Rosa County food distribution event set for Sept. 30
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A large-scale food distribution is coming to Santa Rosa County next week, with organizers expecting to hand out roughly 30,000 pounds of food to residents in need. The event takes place Wednesday, September 30th, from 9 a.m. to 1 p.m. at Welcome Assembly of God Church (8581 Welcome Church Rd, Milton). It's free and open to the public. State…
item.content:encoded:
A large-scale food distribution is coming to Santa Rosa County next week, with organizers expecting to hand out roughly 30,000 pounds of food to residents in need.

The event takes place Wednesday, September 30th, from 9 a.m. to 1 p.m. at Welcome Assembly of God Church (8581 Welcome Church Rd, Milton). It's free and open to the public.

State Representative Michelle Salzman is partnering with several local organizations for the effort, including Be the Miracle, Santa Rosa County Sheriff Bob Johnson's office, Welcome Assembly of God Church, and Feeding the Gulf Coast. "Access to nutritious food is essential for strong and healthy communities," Salzman said in a statement, noting the collaborative approach ensures families throughout Northwest Florida have support during times of food insecurity.

Be the Miracle founder Tim Chandler emphasized the community-wide effort behind the initiative. "It's the generosity and collaboration of organizations and leaders across Santa Rosa County that allows us to reach even more families," he said. The partnership reflects a shared commitment to making sure no family in the county has to face food insecurity alone.

item.title: USPS Unveils Diwali Stamp Celebrating Festival of Lights
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The U.S. Postal Service is marking the Hindu festival of Diwali with a new Forever stamp featuring a vibrant rangoli design, the traditional floor pattern created with colored powders and flower petals that symbolizes good fortune. The stamp showcases an intricate rangoli created by artist Sangita Bhutada, who has been crafting the designs for…
item.content:encoded:
The U.S. Postal Service is marking the Hindu festival of Diwali with a new Forever stamp featuring a vibrant rangoli design, the traditional floor pattern created with colored powders and flower petals that symbolizes good fortune.

The stamp showcases an intricate rangoli created by artist Sangita Bhutada, who has been crafting the designs for nearly 30 years. The artwork displays blues, oranges, greens, reds and whites set against a purple background. The stamp will be sold in panes of 20 and will always equal the current First-Class Mail 1-ounce price.

Diwali, also known as Deepavali, is one of the most important annual Hindu celebrations, typically observed over five days in autumn. This year's main festival day falls on November 8. The celebration marks the triumph of good over evil, with families creating rangolis in and around their homes during the five-day observance.

The stamp's first-day-of-issue ceremony is scheduled for Wednesday, October 21, from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. ET at the Embassy of India in Washington, D.C., with a ceremonial unveiling and reception at 6 p.m. ET. Customers can purchase the stamp through usps.com, by calling 844-737-7826, by mail, or at Post Office locations nationwide.

item.title: Pensacola Beach Chamber Lines Up Fall Events, Taste of the Beach Tickets Available
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Pensacola Beach Chamber of Commerce is ramping up its fall calendar with several signature events designed to draw visitors and give local businesses a spotlight in the coming weeks. Taste of the Beach, one of the chamber's marquee events, is still accepting ticket purchases for three experiential offerings. The Sunset Cruise features an…
item.content:encoded:
The Pensacola Beach Chamber of Commerce is ramping up its fall calendar with several signature events designed to draw visitors and give local businesses a spotlight in the coming weeks.

Taste of the Beach, one of the chamber's marquee events, is still accepting ticket purchases for three experiential offerings. The Sunset Cruise features an evening on Santa Rosa Sound with an open bar and entertainment, followed by heavy appetizers and cocktails at Baja Coastal Kitchen. For a multi-restaurant experience, the VIP Trolley Dinner takes guests to several of Pensacola Beach's top restaurants, while the Brunch Trolley Experience begins with a welcome mimosa at the Visitors Center before moving to three beach restaurants, each with a cocktail pairing.

This Thursday, the Pensacola Beach Chamber is hosting a Joint Business After Hours with the Gulf Breeze Chamber, sponsored by Bamboo Willie's. The event is designed to help chamber members expand their professional networks and reconnect with peers. Meanwhile, the free summer concert series continues tonight at Casino Beach's Gulfside Pavilion, where the Knee Deep Band—a high-energy variety act covering everything from Motown to reggae—will perform from 7 to 9 p.m.

Looking ahead to October, the chamber is calling for vendors for Beach-O-Ween on Friday, October 16 at the Pensacola Beach Boardwalk. Last year's event drew over 1,000 children and families. Chamber members interested in setting up a booth, running a game, or handing out candy can promote their business while contributing to a community Halloween celebration. For more details on any chamber event, visit visitpensacolabeach.com or call the Santa Rosa Island Authority at 850-932-2257.

The advisory means beachgoers should avoid swimming in that area until water conditions improve and testing shows it's safe…
item.content:encoded:
Swimmers in the Orange Beach area need to be aware of a new precaution: the Alabama Department of Public Health has issued a swimming advisory for Wolf Bay after water quality testing came back showing concerning results.

The advisory means beachgoers should avoid swimming in that area until water conditions improve and testing shows it's safe again. Poor water quality can pose health risks to swimmers, particularly for young children, elderly people, and those with weakened immune systems.

Wolf Bay, a popular recreation spot near Orange Beach, is about an hour's drive from Pensacola. While it's outside our immediate area, many Gulf Coast residents visit the Alabama beaches regularly. The Alabama Department of Public Health typically lifts such advisories once water samples meet safe standards, though the timeline can vary depending on conditions.

item.title: Fairhope Army vet's ashes found in storage unit, returned to family

item.content:encoded: A Fairhope Army veteran's remains have been reunited with his family after a remarkable discovery in a storage unit that was auctioned off several months ago. The ashes of Steve Glatfelter, along with a folded American flag and three shell casings, were found among the contents of the unit. The discovery eventually led to the ashes being returned to Glatfelter's granddaughter, according to WKRG News 5. The find highlights how personal items of significant emotional and historical value can sometimes end up in unexpected places when storage units go unpaid and are liquidated through auction.

item.title: Judge Judy Reflects on 30-Year Career, Passes Torch to Son Adam
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Judge Judy Sheindlin is reflecting on three decades on the bench as she steps back from her iconic television courtroom role. In an interview with CBS Mornings, the legendary jurist discussed how her long career changed public perception of the justice system and helped establish legal television as a cultural staple. Sheindlin's show became one…
item.content:encoded:
Judge Judy Sheindlin is reflecting on three decades on the bench as she steps back from her iconic television courtroom role. In an interview with CBS Mornings, the legendary jurist discussed how her long career changed public perception of the justice system and helped establish legal television as a cultural staple.

Sheindlin's show became one of the most-watched court programs in television history, bringing real cases and her no-nonsense judicial style into millions of homes. Her direct approach and quick wit made her a recognizable figure across generations of viewers.

Now, Sheindlin is passing her role to her son, Adam, who will continue the family's courtroom legacy. The transition marks the end of an era for one of television's longest-running and most successful judicial personalities, while opening a new chapter for the next generation of the Sheindlin family in the legal entertainment space.

item.content:encoded:
President Trump addressed world leaders at the United Nations General Assembly in New York City on Tuesday, using the platform to advocate for artificial intelligence to be formally designated as "super intelligence."

During his remarks to the assembly, Trump made the case for the terminology shift as nations grapple with how to define and regulate rapidly advancing AI technology on the global stage.

The president's UN appearance also included announcements regarding international trade and development deals, including a separate agreement involving Greenland that he is set to sign. The specific details and terms of the Greenland deal were not immediately disclosed during his UN address.

item.title: Cuba Walks Out During Trump's UN Speech on Freedom

Trump told the assembly that freedom would be coming to Cuba, a statement that prompted the Cuban representatives to leave the chamber. The walkout underscores the…
item.content:encoded:
Cuba's delegation to the United Nations walked out Tuesday during President Trump's address to the General Assembly, in a show of protest over his remarks about freedom on the island.

Trump told the assembly that freedom would be coming to Cuba, a statement that prompted the Cuban representatives to leave the chamber. The walkout underscores the ongoing diplomatic tension between the United States and Cuba, a relationship that has remained strained through multiple administrations.

The incident marks the latest in a series of confrontations between the two nations at the international stage. Cuba has long objected to U.S. policies toward the island, including trade embargoes and restrictions on travel and commerce. Trump's comments about Cuba's future political direction appear to have crossed a line for the Cuban delegation.

The walkout reflects deep disagreements over governance and human rights issues between Washington and Havana, with no immediate signs of diplomatic resolution.

item.title: Birth Order Study Raises Questions Over Missing Low-Income Families
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A new study examining links between birth order and disease risk has drawn scrutiny from researchers over who was included in the analysis. The research excluded uninsured families and those on Medicaid, potentially skewing results and limiting what the findings can tell us. The study looked at connections between a child's position in the…
item.content:encoded:
A new study examining links between birth order and disease risk has drawn scrutiny from researchers over who was included in the analysis. The research excluded uninsured families and those on Medicaid, potentially skewing results and limiting what the findings can tell us.

The study looked at connections between a child's position in the family—whether they're firstborn, middle, or youngest—and their susceptibility to various diseases. While the research produced measurable results, experts point out that leaving out lower-income families fundamentally compromises the validity of those conclusions.

"A more complete picture would require including all income levels in future research," researchers cautioned. Without data from uninsured and Medicaid-eligible populations, the study may only reflect patterns among insured, higher-income families—a significant limitation when trying to draw broad conclusions about disease risk across the general population.

The findings underscore a broader challenge in medical research: ensuring study populations are representative enough to produce reliable, applicable results. Experts say future investigations into birth order and health outcomes should make inclusive recruitment and diverse income representation a priority from the start.
